subject: dog paws
title: What If You Never Trimmed Your Dog's Nails?

scenes.text: What if you never trimmed your dog's nails? The nail isn't the only thing that keeps growing.
After a couple of months untrimmed, the nails hit the ground first, pushing the toes up and twisting them.
The foot splays and loses grip, so your dog shifts its weight back, overloading its hind leg joints.
Over months, the quick, the living core full of nerve endings, grows longer inside the nail.
Dewclaws never touch the ground, so they never wear down. Left alone, they can grow into the skin.
The twist: a longer quick means you can't just cut it all off. Only many small trims push it back.

description:
What if you never trimmed your dog's nails? Overgrown nails push and twist the toes, splay the foot and shift weight onto the hind legs, while the living quick grows longer inside the nail.
Dewclaws, which never touch the ground, can grow into the skin. Regular trims make the quick recede again.
